title: Gaussian-augmented bosonic matrix-product states: theory and applications
abstract: We propose and analyze the structure of a family of bosonic quantum many-body states that have the following features: (i) they include all pure Gaussian states and finite-dimensional matrix-product states as subclasses; (ii) their expectation values can be efficiently computed, allowing them to be used, among other things, for variational calculations; (iii) they admit exact parent Hamiltonians expressed as simple functions of the bosonic creation and annihilation operators.
summary: The paper introduces Gaussian-augmented bosonic Matrix Product States (GA-BMPS) as a comprehensive variational ansatz for strongly interacting bosonic many-body systems. This framework efficiently computes expectation values and unifies several known state representations, providing a powerful tool for theoretical studies in condensed matter and quantum optics.
main_problem: Developing a unified, efficient variational framework for describing strongly-interacting quantum many-body bosonic systems beyond perturbative regimes.
main_result: The Gaussian-augmented bosonic matrix-product states (GA-BMPS) provide a rich ansatz that unifies pure Gaussian states and finite-dimensional MPS while allowing for efficient computation of expectation values and admitting simple parent Hamiltonians.
method: The authors propose the GA-BMPS ansatz, combining passive linear unitaries with infinite-dimensional bosonic MPS components to represent the quantum state vector.
model_or_system: The focus is on bosonic quantum many-body systems, modeled on a 1D lattice of N sites, which can apply to condensed matter or quantum optics problems. The framework aims to overcome limitations of standard MPS methods in bosonic contexts.
key_observables: Expectation values of local operators $\langle O angle$, characterized by one- and two-point correlation functions ($\Gamma_{ij}, r_i$).
important_parameters: The convergence condition for the transfer matrix is $ho(K) < 1/2$. The ansatz involves bond dimensions $D$ and auxiliary dimensions $d$.
main_assumptions: For simplicity, the analysis often assumes uniform tensors; the framework relies on combining Gaussian unitary transformations with MPS structures.
paper_structure: The paper introduces GA-BMPS as a unifying ansatz, details its construction via combination of unitaries and MPS components, proves computational tractability for expectation values using transfer matrices, establishes equivalences between different state representations (e.g., exponential vs. photon-added), and finally constructs the parent Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful mathematical tools to simulate complex bosonic quantum systems that are difficult to handle with standard tensor network methods due to the nature of bosonic operators.
